title: What is known about 1RB0RD_1RC0LF_0LA0RB_1RE---_1LB1RA_0LE0LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RD_1RC0LF_0LA0RB_1RE---_1LB1RA_0LE0LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine is now reduced exactly to a small one: a wall of n seven-cell words that only counts, and a data word at the fixed end of the tape. One cycle is a visit to the data followed by seven sweeps of the wall; the seven sweeps are proved in Lean for every n and never look at the data. What the visits do to the data is an odometer-like counter whose digits have periods 5, 3, 2, 2, 5, 3, 3, 5, 3, … with no rule yet for the periods of new digits, and that is what a proof would need.
The reduced machine ran 750,000,000 cycles, which is 1.4·10<sup>20</sup> steps of the real machine, without halting; the data word is then 423 cells long.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The wall cycle, for every n
claims.text: Cut the tape between cells 12 and 13. Left of the cut: n words 1001111, then 0100 111111 and two more cells; right of the cut: the data R. If the head comes back from the data onto cell 12 in state B or F, reading 1 with a 1 on its left, then 168(n−1)+575 steps later the head is on the first data cell in state E, the wall has n+3 words, the two cells are 0 1 again and R is untouched. This is Z(n) → Z(n+3).

claims.title: Blank tape reaches Z(7)
claims.text: After 2,035 steps from blank tape the configuration is Z(7, R) with data R = 01010000010010001001.

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweep
claims.text: For every n and any tape around: the head crosses the wall of 7-cell words in each of its forms, rewriting every word the same way.

claims.title: No halt in 750,000,000 cycles (1.4·10<sup>20</sup> steps)
claims.text: c/edge.c runs the machine step by step on the data and jumps over the seven sweeps with the Lean rule. It stops if the head ever touches the wall in a way the rule does not cover; that never happened. Its step counts agree with the plain machine on the first 106 cycles (3·106 steps, py/check_edge.py) and on 123 cycles between steps 6·108 and 7·108. After 750,000,000 cycles the wall has 2,250,000,007 words and the data 423 cells.

claims.title: Every prefix of the data is periodic
claims.text: Over cycles 50,000 to 300,000 the first k data cells repeat with an exact period, for every k up to 120: period 5 (k ≤ 7), 15, 30, 60, 300, 900, 2,700, 13,500, 40,500. Each new stretch of cells multiplies the period by 2, 3 or 5.

claims.title: A mixed-radix odometer
claims.text: How deep the head goes into the data in a cycle follows the same pattern: it turns at cell 16 in exactly one cycle out of 5, at each of 22, 25, 28, 31 in one out of 15, at each of 33, 34, 35, 40 in one out of 30, and so on (counted over 10<sup>7</sup> cycles). The data length grows like the logarithm of the cycle number, about 42 cells per factor 10. No rule is known for the period of the next digit, and nothing here is proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts only on A> 1 0 (1 1 0)k 1 1 1-like patterns (state D reading 1), and by the wall cycle such a pattern can only arise inside the data word. A proof of non-halting needs an invariant for the data word, i.e. a description of the odometer digits that covers the new digits made at the far end.

check: gcc -O2 -o edge holdouts/1RB0RD_1RC0LF_0LA0RB_1RE---_1LB1RA_0LE0LF/c/edge.c && ./edge 10000000     # 2.5e16 steps in a few seconds; more cycles for more

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. But the machine can be cut in two: a wall of seven-cell words that grows by three words per cycle and does nothing else, and a short data word at the fixed end that behaves like the odometer of a car with wheels of 5, 3 and 2 positions. The wall part is proved in Lean; the odometer is where the open question lives.

facts.text: Seven sweeps of the wall in 168(n−1)+575 steps, for every n and any data, proved in Lean.
No halt in 750,000,000 cycles of the reduced machine.
Exact periods of the first cells of the data word.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 41,969 cells (30,639 left of the start, 148 right), with a density of 1s of 0.649.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A wall that only counts, and a data word
html: From step 2,035 on, the tape always has the same layout. On the left a wall of n copies of the word 1001111. Then twelve cells that are almost constant, 0100 111111 and two more. Then, from cell 13 on (cell 0 is where the head started), a data word. Call Z(n, R) the moment the head stands on the first data cell in state E, with 0 1 just left of it, a wall of n words and data R.

From Z(n, R) the head works on the data for a while, a few hundred steps. Sooner or later it comes back over the cut in state B or F. Then it sweeps the whole wall seven times, there and back, rewriting every word on each pass, and returns to the cut. At that moment the tape is Z(n+3, R'): three more words in the wall, and a data word R' that the seven sweeps did not touch. That is one cycle.

The seven sweeps take exactly 168(n−1)+575 steps. Lean checks this for every n and every data word at once (cycle_B, cycle_F), using one shift rule per pass of the head over the wall. So the wall is a clock and nothing more. Whether the machine halts depends only on the sequence of data words R → R' → R'' …

Almost all the running time goes into the wall: a cycle costs 168 n steps there and a few hundred in the data. Jumping over the wall with the Lean rule, c/edge.c runs ten million cycles in a few seconds. That is 2.5·1016 steps of the real machine.

sections.heading: An odometer with wheels of 5, 3 and 2
html: In each cycle the head goes into the data up to some cell and turns back. How far it goes is very regular. Counted over ten million cycles:

the head turns at cellhow often
161 in 5
22, 25, 28, 311 in 15 each
33, 34, 35, 401 in 30 each
4611 in 60
5313 in 300
59, 62, 64, 65, 69, 72, 78, 8413 in 900 each
86 or beyondabout 1 in 17 in total

This is how an odometer behaves: the first wheel moves every time, and passes a tick to the next wheel once per turn. Here the first wheel has 5 positions, so one cycle in five the head stops at cell 16 and the rest of the data is left alone. The next wheels have 3 and 2 positions, and so on.
The same shows in the data itself. Look only at the first k cells of the data word, cycle after cycle. They repeat with an exact period:

first k cellsperiod, in cycles
1–75
8–1815
19–3330

38–44300
45–73900
74–1042,700
105–11113,500
112–12040,500

Each new stretch of cells multiplies the period by 2, 3 or 5. The far end of the data is reached only when all wheels roll over together, which gets rarer and rarer. Then the data grows by a few cells and a new wheel appears. The data length grows like the logarithm of the number of cycles, about 42 cells for every factor of ten.

sections.heading: No rule for the next wheel
html: A real odometer has identical wheels, and a machine with identical wheels is a counter that the standard methods prove to run forever. Here the wheels differ: the periods multiply by 5, 3, 2, 2, 5, 3, 3, 5, 3, … with no pattern found so far. What a new wheel looks like depends on the state of all the old ones at the moment it is made.

The machine can halt in one way only: state D reading a 1, which needs a pattern like 1 0 1 1 1 under the head in state A. By the wall cycle, that could only happen inside the data word. A proof that it never happens needs a description of every data word that can occur, and for that one needs the rule for the wheels.
The reduced machine has run 750,000,000 cycles, 1.4·1020 steps of the real machine, without halting. The tables above come from the same runs. They are measurements, not theorems.

family: bouncer with a mixed-radix odometer at the fixed end
summary: Exact reduction: a wall of n words 1001111 plus a data word; the head leaves the data, sweeps the wall seven times in 168(n-1)+575 steps and comes back with n+3 (proved in Lean for every n), so only the data word matters. The data behaves like an odometer with digits of period 5, 3, 2, ...; no halt in 750,000,000 cycles (1.4e20 steps).
